readout_other: round-window recording of cochlear microphonic and N1 auditory-nerve response
direction_notes: Pulsed 5 MHz ultrasound applied to the dura evoked auditory-nerve (N1) responses and cochlear microphonics in all cats, attributed to radiation-pressure transients heard via bone conduction.
safety_notes: Brain tissue was reported as not observably heated with pulses under 70 microseconds.

exposures.label: 5 MHz pulses against dura over temporal cortex

target.label: dura over the right temporal cortex

device.manufacturer: in-house (0.6-cm PZT disk); one experiment used Panametrics
device.model: 0.6-cm-diam 5-MHz lead zirconate titanate disk in plastic tube

timing.protocol_description: Brief 5-MHz pulses of 10-70 microseconds (about 30 W/cm2 peak) repeated at 10 per second, 200-4000 responses averaged; stimulus series bracketed by tone-pip or click comparison series. Pulse width was varied at constant amplitude.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Auditory-nerve responses were elicited by ultrasound in each of the six cats tested.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: In this study, we measured auditory responses in cats produced by brief pulses of 5- MHz ultrasonic energy from a transducer placed against the dura mater.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.isppa_w_: The averaged round-window response in one cat to a 5-MHz, 68-μs ultrasound pulse, of 30 $\scriptstyle { \mathbf { W } } / \cos ^ { 2 }$ peak intensity applied to the dura over the right temporal cortex, is shown in Fig. 1.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: These pulses are somewhat longer (10-70μs) and more intense
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: followed by a series of ultrasonic pulses (also at $1 0 \ { \mathsf { s } } ^ { - 1 } )$

flags.reason: Peak intensity of about 30 W/cm2 at the dura; domain not stated; power measured by radiation balance in one setup (about 20% error).
Pulse width varied between 10 and 70 microseconds across stimuli; recorded as range.
Each stimulus is a single brief pulse; no train duration stated.
Home-made transducer; one experiment used a Panametrics immersion transducer that was reported as inadequate.
The study is about auditory responses; comparisons with tones and a cat with broken malleus used as tests of the route, not as a control.
